observations: A white, dust-covered dry pressing iron (non-steam type) photographed on a tiled floor.
The power cord shows heavy wear, fraying, and what appears to be exposed bare wire strands near the plug connection at the iron body.
The plug itself appears to be a standard 2-pin type, also showing some wear at the cord entry.
No brand name, logo, or model number is visible anywhere on the iron body.
The sole plate (bottom pressing surface) is not visible in this photo, so its condition cannot be assessed.
No video or photo evidence of the iron being plugged in or heating is provided.

claims.claim: A used dry pressing iron that is still working is available for sale.
claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows only a static image of the iron with no plug-in test, heating demonstration, or video clip to confirm function.

risks.risk: Frayed/exposed wiring at the cord-to-iron junction could mean an electrical safety hazard or indicate the cord needs replacement before safe use.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the cord junction at the iron body and at the plug, clearly showing insulation condition.
risks.if_unproven: priced as needing cord repair/replacement due to visible fraying

risks.risk: Claim of 'still working' cannot be confirmed from a still photo.
risks.proof: A short video clip of the iron plugged in, showing the indicator light or heat being generated (e.g. water droplet sizzle test).

risks.risk: Condition of the sole plate (scratches, pitting, residue buildup) is unknown and affects ironing performance and price.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the underside/sole plate of the iron.
risks.if_unproven: priced as worst case (damaged/scratched sole plate)

risks.risk: No brand/model visible, so comparables for pricing are generic rather than brand-specific, which may undervalue or overvalue versus the real item.
risks.proof: A photo of any brand label, nameplate, or embossed markings on the iron body.

proof_requests: A short video of the iron plugged in and heating up, demonstrating it works.
A close-up photo of the cord at both the iron junction and the plug end to assess wiring safety.
A photo of the sole plate (bottom surface) of the iron.
A photo of any brand or model marking, if present.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a used dry pressing iron, but the unverified 'working' claim and visibly frayed cord mean it must be priced at worst case (non-working, needs rewiring) until proof is supplied.
